subject: Re: Redwood onboarding & procurement path — PO vs Marketplace / exception needed
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jayne Smith <jayne.smith@acme-corp.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood onboarding & procurement path — PO vs Marketplace / next steps

Hi Jayne —

Great speaking with you earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery:

- Pilot scope: 3 LLM endpoints for customer support summarization, expected monthly usage ~150k tokens.
- Target start: July 15 for a 90-day pilot.
- Commercial path: you mentioned finance typically requires AWS Marketplace purchases but procurement also will sometimes do PO-based invoicing for strategic vendors. We need to confirm which route Acme prefers for this pilot (Marketplace vs PO/invoice vs card).

Can you confirm the following so we can route internally?
1) Does Acme allow payments via corporate card for pilot-level spends (~$10–25k)?
2) If card is not allowed, would you prefer AWS Marketplace (credit card through marketplace) or a standard Acme PO/invoice?
3) Are there any prepay or vendor onboarding requirements (W-9, bank info, vendor setup timelines) we should expect?

If Acme cannot issue POs for SaaS vendors (some customers do that), we have a couple fallback options I can propose — acceptance via AWS Marketplace, a prepay invoice, or an internal exception for card payment for pilot deals under $25k. If you can share the procurement contact or policy snippet, I’ll put together the right ask to finance.

Attaching a one-page mutual action plan and a short marketplace onboarding note for context.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this scheduled.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0187

Attachments: Mutual-Action-Plan.xlsx (Excel), Redwood-Marketplace-Onboarding.pdf (PDF)

From: Jayne Smith <jayne.smith@acme-corp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Finance Team <procurement@acme-corp.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood onboarding & procurement path — PO vs Marketplace / next steps

Ben —

Thanks for the recap and the MAP. Quick answers from procurement side:

- Acme generally routes cloud and SaaS purchases through AWS Marketplace when possible. That path is preferred because it attaches spend to our cloud account.
- Corporate card purchases are allowed only for expense-type vendors; we do not use corporate cards for multi-month SaaS subscriptions above $5k/month without special approval.
- We do issue POs/invoices, but only for vendors who have completed our vendor onboarding (W-9, bank details) and meet our vendor risk checks; onboarding typically takes 2–3 weeks.

Two potential blockers for the July 15 start:
1) Our policy requires a vendor to be in the vendor registry to accept POs/invoices — if Redwood is not already onboarded we would need to run that.
2) For pilot-sized spend, our procurement prefers Marketplace; however if Redwood is not listed on AWS Marketplace for the product SKU we plan to purchase, we can't route quickly.

We can do one of the following (your preference):
A) Purchase via AWS Marketplace (fastest if Redwood is listed).
B) Card payment for an initial one-time prepay up to $25k if Redwood is willing to accept a one-time prepay and provide an invoice/receipt. This requires finance approval but is doable.
C) Begin vendor onboarding now and issue a PO/invoice — this will push the timetable ~2–3 weeks.

I’ll cc’ed procurement so they have visibility. If you can confirm whether Redwood supports Marketplace SKUs or whether you can accept a prepay invoice, we’ll route the appropriate internal approvals.

Best,
Jayne
Procurement Manager, Acme Corp
jayne.smith@acme-corp.com

Thanks Jayne — that helps a lot. Short answers:

- Redwood is available on AWS Marketplace (we have consolidated SKUs for our hosted API and dedicated offerings). I’ve attached the marketplace onboarding note with the quick steps.
- We can accept a one-time prepay invoice for pilot spend up to $25k. If Acme prefers prepay, we can generate a DocuSign-ready invoice that you can route to finance for payment; we’ll mark the order applied toward the pilot.
- Vendor onboarding (W-9/bank) is standard and we’ll provide the docs immediately if you want to pursue PO/invoice.

If the fastest path is Marketplace, choose that and I’ll send the exact SKU to purchase. If you need prepay, reply with the billing contact and I’ll spin up the invoice and get legal to confirm terms.

I’m also going to escalate internally to request a short-term exception for card payments for pilot deals under $25k in case Acme needs that route — looping in Marissa (CS) and Rishi (Legal) on this thread.

Next steps (pick one):
- "Marketplace": send me the internal SKU and I’ll confirm listing + provide purchase link.
- "Prepay": send billing contact and PO number (if required on invoice) and I’ll generate DocuSign invoice.
- "PO": initiate onboarding and I’ll provide vendor forms.

Thanks —
Ben

Jayne / team —

Quick update from legal/finance: we can support two paths for the pilot:

1) AWS Marketplace purchase (preferred) — we will confirm SKU and provide the purchase link by EOD today. Marketplace purchases are straightforward and attach to Acme's AWS account.

2) One-time prepay invoice up to $25k — legal has approved a standard invoice + receipt flow for pilots <= $25k without requiring a fully executed SOW. Finance requests that the invoice references PO number if Acme generates one; otherwise we can accept payment without a PO. We will provide a DocuSign invoice (attached template).

We cannot change our standard net terms for pilot invoices; prepay will be upfront and applied against usage. If Acme later wants invoice/PO billing on a committed contract, we can run vendor onboarding and move to standard invoiced terms (Net 30) once vendor registration is complete.

Ben — please send the billing contact and confirm whether Acme will do Marketplace or prepay. Jayne — if you choose prepay, please provide the billing name, email, and any PO number to include on the invoice.

Thanks —
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
